items.title: ‘The Unknown’ Director Arthur Harari Says AI Is a ‘Slippery Slope,’ Though He ‘Had to Use Deepfake Tool’ for Léa Seydoux Double Scene: ‘There Was a Human Behind It’
items.excerpt: 'The Unknown' filmmaker Arthur Harari says AI is 'slippery slope,' though he says he used a deepfake tool for a scene where Léa Seydoux kisses herself.
items.rationale: A concrete on-set use of a deepfake tool by an AI-skeptic auteur: how a face-swap was used for a double scene, with a human performer behind it.

items.rationale: A major Korean short-film festival opens a dedicated AI competition with live submissions, the opposite of the ban-AI moves at other festivals and something filmmakers can enter now.

items.title: Can Dubai’s $1 Million AI Film Award Help AI Cinema Be Taken Seriously?
items.excerpt: As Dubai’s AI Film Award returns for its second edition, the region bears witness to what happens when an AI film prize starts being taken seriously.
items.rationale: The largest AI film prize returns for its second edition. It shows where prize money for AI filmmakers is concentrating and was not covered before (distinct from the 11-12 Higgsfield prize).
